sections.h2: Which Pitt County office handles my property tax?
sections.html:
Pitt County Tax Administration, in Greenville, lists, appraises and assesses real and personal property and collects current and past-due taxes. Its mailing address for appeals is PO Box 43, Greenville, NC 27835-0043, and the Board of Equalization and Review notice gives 252-902-3400 as the phone number.

The county splits its work into divisions you will meet if you file anything. The Real Property Division handles builder exemptions, the Business Personal Property Division handles farm equipment and similar items, and a Tax Relief Division takes applications for the exemption and deferral programs. The county publishes a tax relief email address for questions about those programs.

  • Appeals: formal appeal form and the Board of Equalization and Review clerk.
  • Relief: the Tax Relief Division, by email or in writing to the assessor.
  • Billing and payments: ask Tax Administration for current payment methods.

Ask Tax Administration which taxing jurisdictions bill a given parcel, since a house inside a town may carry more than one bill.

sections.h2: When does Pitt County revalue property?
sections.html:
Pitt County's schedule of values took effect January 1, 2024, and the county says it stays in force until the next revaluation in 2028. Between those years, changes and improvements are appraised under the same statutory standards.

The Schedule of Values is a manual of rates, value ranges and guidelines that the board of commissioners must approve. It covers adjustments for construction types and market conditions and land valuation schedules. Property is appraised at market value, which the Machinery Act defines as the price a willing and financially able buyer and seller would agree on, neither under compulsion and both reasonably informed (G.S. 105-286 sets the reappraisal cycle).

State law also requires a review in the fourth year after a reappraisal. At that point a county looks at whether values need uniform percentage adjustments for categories or areas, instead of reappraising individual parcels. Ask the Pitt assessor whether any such adjustment is planned before the 2028 revaluation.

sections.h2: How do I appeal a Pitt County assessment?
sections.html:
File a formal appeal with the Board of Equalization and Review. The county says you may submit an appeal from January 1 until the board formally adjourns for the year, typically in April or May.

The board is a citizen body appointed by the county commissioners. It is the first level of review, and it hears evidence from both the owner and the assessor's office. Grounds the county names include overvaluation against market value, unequal assessment compared with similar properties, and factual errors in the property record.

Pitt County 2026 board schedule, as posted on the county board page

Bring recent sales of similar homes, a professional appraisal, and photographs of conditions. You can speak yourself or authorize someone to represent you. The county's form page warns that appeals filed after adjournment are untimely and will not be heard by Tax Administration. Dates move from year to year, so read the notice for the year you are in.

If you disagree with the board's decision, an appeal to the state Property Tax Commission must be filed in writing within 30 days after the decision notice is mailed, with a copy to the assessor (G.S. 105-290).

sections.h2: What property tax relief does Pitt County list?
sections.html:
The county relief page covers senior and disabled homeowners, disabled veterans, farmland, builders, nonprofits and vehicle owners. The homestead programs are for owners who live in the home as a primary residence.

  • Elderly or disabled exclusion: removes the greater of $25,000 or 50% of the appraised value of the dwelling and up to one acre. The page prints an income limit of $39,900 for 2027, based on 2026 income.
  • Circuit breaker: caps tax at 4% of income at or below $39,900 and 5% from $39,901 to $59,850 for 2027, with the rest deferred as a lien.
  • Disabled veteran exclusion: the first $45,000 of appraised value, for an honorably discharged veteran with a 100% total and permanent service-connected disability, or an unmarried surviving spouse.

Apply on Form AV-9 to the Pitt County Tax Assessor between January 1 and June 1 of the tax year. Late requests filed June 2 through December 31 may be considered with a documented reason and go to the Board of Equalization and Review. After December 31 they cannot be accepted for the current year. The circuit breaker needs a new application every year and all owners on the deed must qualify, and deferred tax for up to three years plus interest comes due if the home is sold or the owner dies.

Farmers can ask about the present-use value program. The county lists minimums of 10 acres for agricultural use, 5 for horticultural use and 20 for forestry under a written plan, and says rollback taxes for the current and up to three prior years apply if land leaves the program.

sections.h2: When are Pitt County taxes due and what is owed at closing?
sections.html:
State law makes real property tax due September 1 and payable without interest through January 5. From January 6, interest adds 2% for the month and three-quarters of 1% a month after (G.S. 105-360). The county notes that a same-day postmark now has to be requested in person at a Postal Service retail office, so do not count on a late mailing.

The lien for a year's tax attaches as of the listing date (G.S. 105-355), so it follows the parcel into a sale. A closing attorney orders a payoff from Tax Administration and pays it from the seller's proceeds.

  • Request the payoff for each parcel and each taxing jurisdiction.
  • Check whether the parcel is in present-use value or a circuit breaker deferral, since rollback can come due on sale.
  • Check that late relief applications, if any, were decided.

A cash sale can close fast, so request the payoff figure early in the contract period.

faqs.q: When is the next Pitt County revaluation?
faqs.a: The county says its schedule of values, effective January 1, 2024, remains in effect until the next revaluation in 2028. Ask Tax Administration to confirm that date.

faqs.q: How do I appeal my Pitt County property value?
faqs.a: File a formal appeal form with the Board of Equalization and Review, which accepts appeals from January 1 until it adjourns, typically in April or May. The clerk can be reached at 252-902-3400.

faqs.q: What is the Pitt County income limit for the elderly exclusion?
faqs.a: The county page prints $39,900 for 2027, based on 2026 income. Applicants must be 65 or totally and permanently disabled, and must own and live in the home as a primary residence.

faqs.q: Can I apply for tax relief after June 1 in Pitt County?
faqs.a: Possibly, since applications filed June 2 through December 31 may be considered with a valid documented reason and are reviewed by the Board of Equalization and Review. Applications after December 31 cannot be accepted for the current year.

faqs.q: What happens to deferred taxes if I sell a Pitt County home?
faqs.a: Circuit breaker deferred taxes for up to three years plus interest become due if the home is sold, the owner dies or it stops being a permanent residence. Present-use value land owes rollback taxes if it leaves the program.
